subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Continuous variation (e.g. human height) is typically caused by:
options: A single gene with two alleles
Many genes acting together (polygenic) plus environmental influence
questions.explain: Continuous variation is polygenic, with many genes and the environment producing a range of phenotypes.

questions.q: The sodium-potassium pump in co-transport maintains a low intracellular Na+ concentration by:
options: actively pumping 3 Na+ out and 2 K+ in using ATP
pumping glucose out of the cell
allowing Na+ to diffuse passively out
questions.explain: The Na+/K+ ATPase actively exports 3 Na+ and imports 2 K+ per ATP, creating the Na+ gradient that powers glucose co-transport.

questions.q: Unlike simple diffusion, the rate of facilitated diffusion reaches a plateau at high concentration gradients because:
options: the transport proteins become saturated, limiting the rate
questions.explain: When all carrier or channel proteins are working at maximum capacity, the number of transport proteins limits the rate, producing a plateau.

questions.q: Cholesterol in the cell membrane functions to:
options: regulate membrane fluidity and stability by sitting between phospholipids
questions.explain: Cholesterol fits between phospholipid tails, restricting their movement to maintain fluidity and mechanical stability across temperatures.

questions.q: Cholesterol contributes to membrane stability at low temperatures by:
options: preventing the phospholipids from packing too closely, so the membrane does not become too rigid and stays fluid
allowing phospholipids to pack tightly and freeze solid
questions.explain: At low temperatures cholesterol stops phospholipids packing tightly together, maintaining fluidity and preventing the membrane becoming too rigid.

questions.q: A red blood cell placed in pure water bursts (haemolysis) because:
options: water enters down a water potential gradient and the cell has no rigid wall to resist swelling
the membrane actively pumps water in
solutes enter the cell by active transport
water leaves the cell by osmosis
questions.explain: Pure water has a higher water potential than the cytoplasm, so water enters by osmosis; lacking a cell wall, the animal cell swells and lyses.

questions.q: Active transport is inhibited by a respiratory poison such as cyanide because:
options: the poison denatures the phospholipid bilayer
it prevents ATP production, removing the energy needed to pump substances against their gradient
questions.explain: Active transport depends on ATP from aerobic respiration; inhibiting respiration removes the energy source, halting the pumping of substances against their gradient.

questions.q: In PCR, the temperature is raised to around 95 degrees C in order to:
options: Separate the two DNA strands by breaking hydrogen bonds
questions.explain: Denaturation at ~95 degrees C breaks the hydrogen bonds, separating the DNA into single strands.

questions.q: Which feature distinguishes RNA from DNA?
options: RNA contains thymine instead of uracil
RNA nucleotides are joined by ester bonds, not phosphodiester bonds
questions.explain: RNA uses the pentose ribose and the base uracil in place of thymine, and is typically single-stranded.

questions.q: Increasing the number of channel and carrier proteins in a membrane would increase the rate of facilitated diffusion only if:
options: the temperature is reduced to zero
there is still a concentration gradient and proteins were previously the limiting factor
the molecules are non-polar and small
questions.explain: More transport proteins raise the rate only when proteins limit it and a gradient remains to drive the movement.

questions.q: During transcription, which enzyme joins RNA nucleotides together to form pre-mRNA?
questions.explain: RNA polymerase catalyses the formation of phosphodiester bonds between RNA nucleotides during transcription.

questions.q: On the leading strand during DNA replication, synthesis is:
options: Continuous, following the replication fork in a 5' to 3' direction
questions.explain: The leading strand template runs 3' to 5' towards the fork, so DNA polymerase synthesises it continuously 5' to 3'.

questions.q: The quaternary structure of haemoglobin refers to:
options: the folding of one polypeptide into a 3D shape
the sequence of amino acids in each chain
the association of four polypeptide subunits each with a haem prosthetic group
the alpha-helical coiling of a single chain
questions.explain: Quaternary structure is the arrangement of multiple polypeptide subunits; haemoglobin has four chains, each bound to a haem group.

questions.q: When a fully turgid plant cell has its pressure potential exactly balancing its solute potential, its water potential is zero, meaning:
options: there is no net movement of water into or out of the cell when surrounded by pure water
questions.explain: At full turgor the inward pressure potential equals the solute potential in magnitude, giving Psi = 0, so no net water movement occurs with pure water outside.

questions.q: Discontinuous variation differs from continuous variation because it:
options: Is always caused by the environment
Falls into distinct, non-overlapping categories controlled by one or few genes
questions.explain: Discontinuous variation gives discrete categories, typically controlled by one or a few genes with little environmental effect.

questions.q: The site of translation in a eukaryotic cell is the:
questions.explain: Translation occurs at ribosomes, where mRNA codons are read to assemble a polypeptide.

questions.q: In a monohybrid cross between two heterozygous parents (Tt x Tt), the expected phenotypic ratio is:
questions.explain: A heterozygous monohybrid cross gives a 3:1 ratio of dominant to recessive phenotypes.

questions.q: A tRNA anticodon is 5'-UAC-3'. The mRNA codon it pairs with is:
questions.explain: Antiparallel complementary base pairing of anticodon 5'-UAC-3' gives codon 5'-GUA-3'.

questions.q: In a sample of double-stranded DNA, 20% of the bases are adenine. The percentage of cytosine is:
questions.explain: By Chargaff's rule A=T=20%, so G+C=60%, and since G=C, cytosine is 30%.

questions.q: After 3 complete cycles of PCR starting from one double-stranded DNA molecule, the number of DNA molecules produced is:
questions.explain: PCR doubles the DNA each cycle, so after 3 cycles there are 2 cubed = 8 molecules.

questions.q: Two cells are in contact: cell A has a water potential of -400 kPa and cell B has -750 kPa. Water will move:
options: not at all because the cells are isolated
from cell A to cell B
from cell B to cell A
in both directions equally with no net movement
questions.explain: Water moves from a higher (less negative) water potential to a lower (more negative) one, i.e. from A (-400) to B (-750).

questions.q: Which feature of the genetic code means each base is part of only one triplet?
questions.explain: In a non-overlapping code each base is read only once, belonging to a single codon.

questions.q: In cats, a coat-colour gene is X-linked with codominant alleles for orange and black, producing tortoiseshell heterozygotes. Tortoiseshell cats are almost always female because:
options: The orange allele is lethal in males
Only females (XX) can carry both alleles at once
questions.explain: Heterozygosity for both X-linked alleles requires two X chromosomes, which normally only females possess.

questions.q: Haemophilia is more common in males than females because:
options: The allele is carried on the Y chromosome
Males have only one X chromosome, so a single recessive allele is expressed
questions.explain: The recessive allele is X-linked, and males (XY) express it with only one copy as they have no second X to mask it.

questions.q: In prokaryotes, unlike eukaryotes, mRNA does not require splicing because:
questions.explain: Prokaryotic genes generally lack introns, so the mRNA is functional without splicing.

questions.q: Reverse transcriptase is used in genetic engineering to:
options: Cut DNA at specific recognition sites
Synthesise complementary DNA (cDNA) from an mRNA template
questions.explain: Reverse transcriptase makes single-stranded cDNA from mRNA, a useful intron-free copy of a gene.

questions.q: Which type of mutation is most likely to alter every amino acid downstream of the mutation site?
options: A substitution at the third base of a codon
A deletion of a single base
questions.explain: A single-base deletion shifts the reading frame, changing all subsequent codons (a frameshift).

questions.q: Adding solute to pure water causes the water potential to:
questions.explain: Solute molecules lower the free energy of water, making the solute (and overall) potential more negative than zero.

questions.q: Which factor would increase the permeability of a cell membrane?
options: An increase in temperature, increasing phospholipid movement and creating gaps
A decrease in temperature, increasing phospholipid order
questions.explain: Higher temperatures increase phospholipid kinetic energy and fluidity, and can denature membrane proteins, increasing permeability.

questions.q: How many different codons are possible using a triplet code of four bases?
questions.explain: With four bases in groups of three, 4 cubed = 64 possible codons.
